title: Reviewer protocol drift: a missing reviewer hidden by a case-variant duplicate verdict (SYNTHETIC)
scientific_question: Illustrative only (invented): did every required reviewer record exactly one verdict on the synthetic sample batch? No real reviewer, person or institution is involved.
claim_tested: Given three required reviewers (syn-reviewer-a, syn-reviewer-b, syn-reviewer-c) and three recorded verdicts, where syn-reviewer-c recorded none and syn-reviewer-b recorded two under spellings that differ only in case and trailing whitespace ('syn-reviewer-b' and 'SYN-Reviewer-B '), science-gate verify with a required reviewer_protocol check reports ABSTAIN with exit code 2, reason PROTOCOL_BROKEN and failure modes exactly [PROTOCOL_DRIFT], and its report names syn-reviewer-c as recording no verdict and syn-reviewer-b as recording more than one. It must not PASS because the number of verdicts equals the number of required reviewers.
falsified_by: The recorded run returning PASS, FAIL or ERROR; an exit code other than 2; a reason other than PROTOCOL_BROKEN; failure_modes other than exactly [PROTOCOL_DRIFT]; or a report.md that lacks any of the must_mention strings.

unresolved_cases: The content of the verdicts (all ACCEPT here) is not judged; the check establishes protocol completeness only.

Reviewer identity is a name string compared after trimming and case folding. One person recording under two unrelated names, or two people sharing a name, cannot be detected, and the verdicts document is not authenticated.
A verdict from a reviewer who is not required is listed as evidence but is not exercised here.
A missing reviewer alone, and a duplicate alone, are not separate entries; this entry combines both.
report.md prints two different row figures: 'Rows examined in scope: 7' (4 sample rows + 3 verdicts) and the pass_requires_examined_rows line, which sums per-check counts. Neither is asserted here.
